investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were written, causing a total contract violation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The pod scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and found no preemption victims, so the agent pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the production-api remote-agents observability check; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with no preemption path available.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150391, pod stuck unscheduled for 145s, check ended at 2026-07-09T15:28:36.164Z — the pod never reached a running state within the eval window.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}); none of the four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were written, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields — orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState — are listed as missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent could return.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: near-identical scheduler message (144s), latencyMs=149935, empty evidenceKeys — a third independent probe attempt hit the same constraint.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the VM was never allocated.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked/zombie VMs that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required node selector, meaning effective schedulable capacity is limited to only 2 nodes; any reduction in those nodes' VM quota immediately causes full unavailability.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs): if cleanup failed on previous runs, VM slots may be held indefinitely, reducing available capacity over time.

QUATERNARY — Cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource; if concurrent workloads or other probes consume those slots simultaneously, the eval window is too narrow for scheduling to succeed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were written, causing a total contract violation.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The pod scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and found no preemption victims, so the agent pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the production-api remote-agents observability check; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-09 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had zero schedulable capacity for kata peer-pod VMs, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes rejecting the pod due to node affinity/selector mismatch. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints and are therefore ineligible regardless of resource availability. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt timed out after ~145 seconds (well within the eval's 420 s outage threshold), preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, state polling, or runtime chat steps. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-level failure.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for remote-agent pods (matching the affinity/selector), and those 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm quota. If the eligible node pool was recently reduced or the affinity rules were tightened, capacity would drop without any application code change.

Tertiary — kata peer-pod infrastructure quota limit not scaled to eval concurrency: the eval suite runs remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime sequentially; if prior runs did not fully clean up peer-pod VMs (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 failed silently), leaked VMs could exhaust the quota.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node NotReady, maintenance drain): one or both affinity-eligible nodes may have been temporarily cordoned or drained, reducing effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to zero for the duration of the eval window.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-runtime (or remote-agent-create) that produces a scheduled pod and returns all required evidence fields would indicate the scheduling failure was transient rather than a sustained capacity problem.

Kubectl describe output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 and used = 0 on the affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was erroneous or the node labels changed mid-run.

Evidence that the 2 affinity-eligible nodes were cordoned, drained, or NotReady during the eval window would shift the cause from quota exhaustion to a node availability event rather than a VM resource limit.

A passing run of remote-agent-create immediately after the failure window with no infrastructure changes would suggest the failure was caused by a transient concurrent workload spike rather than a persistent quota ceiling.

Cluster event logs showing a node scale-up event completing after the eval window would indicate autoscaling was triggered but too slow to serve the eval, pointing to a scaling policy gap rather than a hard quota limit.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity message rather than waiting for the full scheduling timeout.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods remain in Running or Terminating state after each remote-agents eval cycle, catching quota leakage from failed withCleanup calls.

Add a remote-agents node-pool health check that verifies at least one affinity-eligible node is Ready and has non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity, surfacing node pool shrinkage or cordon events before they block agent creation evals.

Consider adding a latency-banded warning eval for remote-agent-create that fires at the warningLatencyMs threshold (240 s) with the scheduler Pending reason, giving earlier signal before the 360 s outage threshold is crossed.
